findings.evidence: Existing root subgroups have `coe_geckRootSubgroupPoints` (GroupScheme.lean:531). The generic `kostantBracketRootSubgroupParam` is never mentioned in AdjacentRoot.lean outside the imported theorems.
findings.fix: Add a `@[simp] coe_geckAdjacentRootSubgroupPoints` that gives the matrix as the image under `LinearMap.toMatrixAlgEquiv` of `kostantBracketRootSubgroupParam`, or define the subgroup directly as that image and derive the commutator form as a theorem.
findings.issue: `geckAdjacentRootSubgroupPoints` is defined as `⁅x_i(a), x_j(1)⁆`, with no lemma identifying its matrix with the base-changed divided-power exponential of `⁅e_i,e_j⁆`, i.e. the image of `kostantBracketRootSubgroupParam`. Without that, the L5 consumer cannot match it against a pinned root subgroup.

findings.evidence: `t.geckAdjacentRootSubgroupPoints ht i j hij hji A a = ⁅t.geckRootSubgroupPoints ht (.inl i) A a, … (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)⁆ := (rfl)` carries `@[simp]`.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` here and put it on the coe/exponential characterization requested above. Keep this as a plain lemma, or state it as the b = 1 case of the commutator relation.
findings.issue: The `@[simp]` on `geckAdjacentRootSubgroupPoints_apply` rewrites the new subgroup into the commutator of simple-root points, so simp erases the new object. That is the wrong normal form for a named root subgroup.

findings.evidence: Both proofs are `simp only [commutatorElement_kostantRootSubgroupParam_eq_bracket …, mul_one]`, the second followed by `map_mul (kostantBracketRootSubgroupParam …)`. Their only uses are in AdjacentRoot.lean's private theorems.
findings.fix: Delete both, and in AdjacentRoot.lean derive `commutator_mul_one`/`commutator_add` directly from `_eq_bracket` (plus `map_mul` of `kostantBracketRootSubgroupParam`).
findings.issue: `commutatorElement_kostantRootSubgroupParam_eq_mul_one` and `commutatorElement_kostantRootSubgroupParam_add_one` (line 155) are public intermediates. Each follows from `commutatorElement_kostantRootSubgroupParam_eq_bracket` (the second also needs `map_mul`), and they exist only to serve the private Geck helpers.

summary: The Geck sum-root subgroup is defined as a commutator with no lemma linking it to the bracket exponential, and its only @[simp] lemma rewrites it back to that commutator. The generic file also exports two redundant intermediate commutator theorems.
